title: Best Places to Visit in Kashmir: A Practical Guide for Your First Trip
subtitle: The places worth your time, when to go, and how to plan without stress on your first trip to Kashmir.
excerpt: Ask ten travelers about Kashmir and you will get ten different favorite spots. Fitting them into the right number of days is where most people get stuck. This guide covers the places worth your time, when to go, and how to plan without stress.

contentSections.heading: Srinagar: Start Here
contentSections.content:
Most Kashmir trips begin in Srinagar, and it deserves at least two nights. Take a shikara ride on Dal Lake early in the morning, when the water is still and the floating vegetable boats are out. Spend one night on a houseboat, even if you usually avoid touristy things. The rooms are cozy, the food is homemade, and people remember it long after the trip.

Set aside an afternoon for the Mughal Gardens. Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh and Chashme Shahi are close enough to see in one go. After that, walk through the old city for shawls, saffron and walnut wood crafts. Bargain politely, and ask what is truly handmade.

contentSections.heading: Gulmarg: Green Meadows or Fresh Snow
contentSections.content: Gulmarg is around two hours from Srinagar by road. The Gulmarg Gondola lifts you high above the slopes, and on a clear day the views are worth the wait in line. Come in winter for skiing and snow play, or in summer for flower-covered meadows and pony rides. Book gondola tickets online in advance, because queues get long in peak season.

contentSections.heading: Pahalgam and Betaab Valley
contentSections.content: Pahalgam sits beside the Lidder River and feels slower and greener than the city. Use it as a base for Betaab Valley, Aru Valley and Chandanwari. Stay two nights if you enjoy easy walks, and give yourself time to just sit by the river with a cup of kahwa.

contentSections.heading: Sonamarg: The Meadow of Gold
contentSections.content: Sonamarg means "meadow of gold," and in late spring the name makes sense. The main draw is the trip toward Thajiwas Glacier, which you can do on foot or by pony. Most travelers visit Sonamarg as a day trip from Srinagar. The road also leads toward Ladakh and can close after heavy snow, so check conditions before you leave.

contentSections.heading: Offbeat Picks: Doodhpathri, Yusmarg and Gurez
contentSections.content: If crowds bother you, Doodhpathri and Yusmarg are calm meadows within a few hours of Srinagar. They suit families and anyone who wants a slow, quiet day. Gurez Valley is remote and beautiful, but it takes more planning. Access rules can change, so confirm permits and road status before you commit.

contentSections.heading: Tulip Garden and the Lakes
contentSections.content: The Tulip Garden in Srinagar blooms roughly from late March to April, though the exact dates shift with the weather. If spring is your plan, ask your tour operator for the current bloom status. For a slower itinerary, Wular Lake and Mansar Lake are peaceful places to break up a long drive.

contentSections.heading: Best Time to Visit Kashmir
contentSections.content: Each season gives you a distinct and memorable experience across the valley:
bulletPoints: Spring (March to May): Tulips in bloom, mild weather, and fewer crowds early on.
Summer (June to August): Green alpine meadows, trekking trails, and comfortable daytime temperatures.
Autumn (September to November): Golden chinar leaves, apple harvests, and crisp clear skies.
Winter (December to February): Deep snow, skiing in Gulmarg, and a serene, quiet Dal Lake.

contentSections.heading: How Many Days Do You Need?
contentSections.content: Five to six days is a comfortable plan for Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg. Four days works if you are happy to move quickly. If you want offbeat places or a relaxed pace, plan for seven days.

contentSections.heading: Quick Travel Tips
contentSections.content: Practical essentials to ensure a seamless holiday in Kashmir:
bulletPoints: Pack layers even in summer, because mountain evenings turn cool quickly.
Carry a valid government photo ID and sufficient cash for small local shops.
Mobile connectivity: Prepaid SIM cards from other Indian states often do not work in Kashmir, so ensure you carry a postpaid connection.
Check official travel advisories and weather forecasts before departing, and start intercity road trips early in the day.

contentSections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
contentSections.content: Key answers for travelers planning their first Kashmir holiday:
bulletPoints: What is the best time to visit Kashmir? April to October suits most travelers for pleasant weather and green meadows. Choose December to February if snow and winter sports are your primary goal.
How many days are enough for Kashmir? Five to six days comfortably covers Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam, and Sonamarg without feeling rushed.

Is Kashmir safe for tourists? Tourism is active and millions of travelers visit safely every year. Conditions can fluctuate, so always check advisories and travel with a reputable, licensed local tour operator.
contentSections.highlightQuote: Kashmir is the kind of place that looks better in person than in any photo. Once you know the best places to visit, the next step is choosing your dates.
